name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
description: An iconic 5th-century rock fortress rising 200m above the plains. Its summit offers panoramic views of jungles, distant hills, and symmetrical water gardens below. The ancient ramparts and Lion's Gate make for dramatic compositions, especially in soft light.
bestTimeToShoot: Sunrise for cooler temps, minimal crowds, and golden light illuminating the rock's reddish hues. Sunset is also beautiful but busier.
droneNotes: Allowed only with Civil Aviation Authority permit. Avoid flying directly over the fortress or crowds, and keep a respectful distance.
recommendedShot: Panoramic view from summit showing symmetrical water gardens and jungle canopy at golden hour

name: Nine Arch Bridge, Ella
description: A picturesque colonial-era railway viaduct hidden in Ella's green highlands. Nine elegant brick arches span a jungle valley, and the sight of the famous blue train crossing this curved bridge is a must-capture shot. Lush tea slopes and misty hills frame the scene.
bestTimeToShoot: Morning (around 8-9 AM) when the train typically passes. Early light adds soft contrast in the valley. Late afternoon offers warmer tones.
droneNotes: Allowed. Drone shots reveal the full curve of the bridge and surrounding jungles. Use caution not to fly too low near the train or over people on the tracks.
recommendedShot: Blue train crossing the curved bridge with misty tea hills in background

name: Galle Fort and Lighthouse
description: A charming 17th-century Dutch fort town on the coast, with cobblestone lanes, colonial architecture, and a scenic lighthouse on the ramparts. Photographers love the blend of old-world charm against the Indian Ocean backdrop - from vibrant street scenes to sunsets over stone walls.
bestTimeToShoot: Late afternoon into sunset. Golden hour light warms the fort's stone and colonial buildings. Sunset often creates fiery skies over the ocean.
droneNotes: Permitted with conditions as a UNESCO site. Avoid flying directly over busy streets or the lighthouse when people are around. Be mindful of local no-fly zones.
recommendedShot: Lighthouse silhouette against fiery sunset sky with ocean waves crashing on ramparts

name: Mirissa & Coconut Tree Hill
description: A postcard-perfect beach town known for its palm-fringed bay and the famous Coconut Tree Hill - a small laterite cliff jutting into the sea, topped with a cluster of tall palm trees. This spot offers a panoramic ocean view with silhouetted palms, especially stunning at dawn or dusk.
bestTimeToShoot: Sunrise at Coconut Tree Hill for calm light and fewer people. December-March is dry season with clear skies and vibrant sunsets.
droneNotes: Allowed. Open coastal area with no special restrictions. Fly in early morning or golden hour for softer light. Watch for ocean winds.
recommendedShot: Silhouetted palm trees on the cliff against colorful sunrise sky with turquoise ocean below

name: Horton Plains & World's End
description: A highland national park of rolling grasslands and cloud forests, ending abruptly at World's End - an 880m sheer cliff with jaw-dropping valley vistas. Photogenic features include mist-shrouded plains at dawn, wildlife like sambar deer grazing, and Baker's Falls.
bestTimeToShoot: Early morning (6-10 AM). Arrive before 10 AM to catch the view before clouds roll in. Best months are December-March for clearer weather.
droneNotes: Not allowed without special permission. Drones are restricted in national parks to avoid disturbing wildlife. Park rangers enforce no-drone rules.
recommendedShot: Panoramic cliff edge view with mist rising from valley and golden morning light

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth, Kandy
description: The holiest Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka, known as Sri Dalada Maligawa, set beside Kandy Lake. Its white walls, golden roof and lake reflections create serene images. Inside are ornate halls and candlelit rituals.
bestTimeToShoot: Evening during the daily puja (prayer offering) around sunset (dusk). Temple interiors glow with lamp light. Early morning gives soft light on outer walls and calm lake reflections.
droneNotes: Not advised. Active religious site in an urban area. Drone flights are generally prohibited over the Temple and palace complex for security and respect.
recommendedShot: Temple exterior reflected in Kandy Lake at blue hour with golden roof illuminated

name: Jaffna Peninsula (Nallur Temple)
description: The far north offers a different cultural palette - Hindu temples with vibrant gopurams, empty lagoons, islands, and colonial remnants. The Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil with its towering candy-colored Dravidian-style tower is a striking subject.
bestTimeToShoot: Morning or late afternoon for soft light on temple exteriors. July-August festival offers incredible photo opportunities. May-September yields clear skies in the north.
droneNotes: Use caution. Not outright banned but some areas near military installations or airports are sensitive. Fly over temples only with permission.
recommendedShot: Colorful gopuram tower against blue sky with devotees at entrance

name: Adam's Peak (Sri Pada)
description: A sacred mountain pilgrimage site (2,243m) with a distinctive conical shape. Photography here is about the journey and the sunrise: long exposure trails of pilgrims' lanterns pre-dawn, and the famed triangular shadow the peak casts over the clouds at sunrise.
bestTimeToShoot: Pre-dawn hike for sunrise at the summit (5:30-6:00 AM). Climb overnight December-April during pilgrimage season. Avoid May-October due to heavy rains.
droneNotes: Generally discouraged. Lies within a sensitive nature reserve and is sacred to multiple religions. Large crowds mean drones are not appropriate during pilgrimage.
recommendedShot: Triangular shadow phenomenon at sunrise with sea of clouds and golden glow over highlands

name: Polonnaruwa Ancient City
description: Sprawling ruins of a medieval capital nestled in greenery - including majestic Buddha statues carved from rock (e.g. Gal Vihara), crumbling stupas, and lily-covered ponds. Photographers love Polonnaruwa for its blend of ancient artistry and jungle overgrowth.
bestTimeToShoot: Early morning (shortly after sunrise) when light is soft and temperatures cooler. Low-angle sunlight highlights stone carvings. June-September is relatively dry.
droneNotes: Allowed with permission. As a UNESCO World Heritage site, obtain approval for drone flights. Fly high enough to frame the complex but avoid going too low over temples or wildlife.
recommendedShot: Gal Vihara reclining Buddha statue with soft morning light accentuating stone textures

name: Stilt Fishermen (Koggala Coast)
description: An iconic Sri Lankan scene - fishermen perched on wooden stilts in the surf, casting lines at dawn or dusk. This traditional practice yields surreal, silhouette-like images. The men balanced on poles with waves and colorful sky behind is quintessential.
bestTimeToShoot: Dawn (5:30-6:30 AM) is ideal. Rising sun behind fishermen creates dramatic backlighting and reflections. Sunset also works with warm hues.
droneNotes: Allowed on open coastline. Keep a good distance so as not to scare the fish or fishermen. Ask permission if close. Some fishermen may expect a small tip.
recommendedShot: Row of silhouetted fishermen on stilts against dramatic orange sunrise with ocean reflections

name: Tea Plantations of Nuwara Eliya
description: Endless emerald tea hills in the highlands, often blanketed in mist. Neatly trimmed tea bushes create layered patterns over rolling terrain. Occasional bright saris of tea pluckers amid the green provide focal points of cultural interest.
bestTimeToShoot: Early morning for mystical mist and soft light. Late afternoon golden hour lights up lush green with warm tones. March-May is prime harvesting season with more activity.
droneNotes: Allowed. Tea estates are generally drone-friendly. Wide aerial shots showcase vast scale and patchwork patterns. Be mindful of not flying over groups of workers without asking.
recommendedShot: Layered tea terraces with morning mist and tea plucker in bright sari as focal point

name: Yala National Park
description: A famed wildlife sanctuary known for leopards, elephants, peacocks, and other fauna against a backdrop of scrub jungle, lagoons, and dunes. Photographically, Yala offers safari scenes akin to an African savannah.
bestTimeToShoot: February-June dry season for frequent wildlife sightings at waterholes. Early morning safaris (6-9 AM) or late afternoon (3-6 PM) are best for active animals and soft lighting.
droneNotes: Not permitted. All national parks prohibit drones without explicit Department of Wildlife permission. Drone noise can distress wildlife. Use telephoto lenses instead.
recommendedShot: Leopard on tree branch with golden afternoon light and dusty savannah backdrop

name: Minneriya National Park
description: A lush park famed for the 'Elephant Gathering' - one of the world's largest wild elephant meet-ups. In dry season, hundreds of elephants congregate on the shores of Minneriya Tank at dusk.
bestTimeToShoot: July-October dry season, with peak elephant counts in August-September. Late afternoon safari (2:30-6:00 PM) for soft golden light. Golden hour backlights elephants and dust for magical silhouettes.
droneNotes: Not allowed. Drones are banned to protect elephants. Park authorities will not permit drone flights with large herds present. Use long lenses instead.
recommendedShot: Herd of elephants silhouetted against sunset sky at Minneriya Tank with dust catching golden light

name: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
description: A UNESCO-listed pristine rainforest - dense, lush, and teeming with endemic flora and fauna. Photogenic features include sunlight filtering through giant tropical leaves, misty forest trails, sparkling streams, and colorful birds like the Sri Lanka blue magpie.
bestTimeToShoot: Morning is best - forest is most alive at sunrise to mid-morning with bird calls and feeding flocks. Go in dry months (January-March, or August) when rain is minimal.
droneNotes: Not allowed. Strictly protected reserve - no drones permitted inside the forest. The canopy is thick with little open space to fly anyway. Focus on ground photography.
recommendedShot: Sunlight shafts filtering through dense canopy with mist and endemic bird perched on branch

name: Diyaluma Falls (Koslanda)
description: Sri Lanka's second-highest waterfall (220m) tumbling down in horsetail leaps to a rocky pool. Spectacular from both the base (full height view) and the top, where natural infinity pools overlook the valley. An adventurous, lesser-crowded spot.
bestTimeToShoot: Dry season January-March for safe access to top pools. Morning is good for soft light and fewer people. Late morning gets sun into the canyon.
droneNotes: Allowed - not in a national park. Drone can capture the full cascade from above. Launch from stable area (top is windy, bottom has spray). Avoid flying directly over swimmers.
recommendedShot: Aerial view of waterfall cascade with natural infinity pools and valley stretching to horizon

name: Anuradhapura Sacred City
description: The vast ruins of an ancient Sinhala civilization, famous for enormous white dagobas rising above the treetops. Photogenic landmarks include Ruwanwelisaya and Jetavanaramaya stupas (among the tallest brick structures in the world), and the sacred Bodhi Tree.
bestTimeToShoot: Early morning for soft light and morning offerings. Late afternoon towards sunset - white dagobas take on golden and pink hues with the setting sun.
droneNotes: Allowed with heavy restrictions. Must have permission to fly as living UNESCO heritage city. Avoid flying during prayer times or over the Bodhi Tree and crowds.
recommendedShot: Giant white stupa (Ruwanwelisaya) glowing in pink sunset light with monks in white robes in foreground
